intent: supplementary architecture components using the current card and first atlas as references
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent production sprite atlas for a modular regional map city. Make ONE new 4 column by 4 row sheet, exactly sixteen isolated cutouts, with broad transparent gutters, no grid or labels.
REFERENCE ROLES: first image (Citadel of Stillness card) defines the Warlord's severe armour-like architecture, three tall blade-prongs bound by a teal horizontal band, red and charcoal materials and oppressive presence. Do NOT copy its low frontal camera, sky, landscape, complete building or whole scene. Second image (previous modular sheet) defines the distant three-quarter overhead map camera and the SMALL door/window/roof scale only. Improve its too-friendly toy-castle treatment: fewer bright cream edges, less generic cottages, more severe vertical stone blades, flat armoured surfaces, deep red roofs, rib-built supports and continuous inhabited galleries. New pieces must connect into long wings at their ends, rather than all being standalone miniature buildings.

Architecture is an inhabited otherworldly armoured body: old ossified ribs and vertebral braces are physically load-bearing, integrated into stone piers and roof ribs. No skull faces, eyes, wounds, gore or people. No loose skeleton decoration. The city must remain useful and inhabited. Material decay is a secondary feature; do not replace the clear architecture with rubble piles. Muted charcoal/slate stone midtones, vermilion and brick-red roof/enamel, worn oxidized teal binding bands. Bone support edges subdued grey ivory, never bright yellow outlines everywhere. Local material colour, no all-over tint or glow. Readable middle values with restrained dark joints. Hard hand-placed pixel clusters, selective engraving/dither, coherent bold forms suitable for tiny map sprites. Upper-left light.

Exact row-major elements:
Row1: one tall narrow straight stone blade-tower with small red vertical inset, a tiny normal-size door at base and a teal binding band midway; a shorter companion blade-tower with roof landing and band at same architectural level; a broken blade-tower with partial upper shaft; one low ossified rib-buttress and stone support.
Row2: a straight EAST-WEST armoured roofed gallery segment with flat joinable end profiles, three tiny ordinary-size bays, red roof and continuous teal band; a straight NORTH-SOUTH gallery segment in the same overhead projection, three tiny bays, same roof/band level; a matching EAST-WEST low rampart section with flat joinable ends; a matching NORTH-SOUTH low rampart section. These are long narrow sections, NOT complete houses with gabled end walls. Each fits about two or three ordinary house widths. They will overlap slightly at their ends.
Row3: an L-shaped gallery junction connecting the two orientations; a T-shaped gallery junction; a modest inhabited gate with its roof/band matching the galleries, NOT an enormous cathedral entrance; one U-shaped three-sided rib-braced court wing, its open court truly transparent.
Row4: partly ruined east-west gallery segment, keeping enough intact end profile to join; partly ruined north-south gallery segment; one low dense terrace of three attached narrow red-roof houses, every doorway at exactly the same scale as the first reference modules; one low broken ossified structural wall segment with slate rubble feet.

Distant three-quarter overhead from the south, roofs visible. Every sprite complete, centred in its own cell with broad transparent margin; do not let tall towers touch edges. TRUE transparent background. No scenic ground, water, sky, diamond bases, paved square plates, scenery or detached shadows. Sparse low rubble may meet alpha at feet. No writing, UI, borders, framing, vignette or emblem overlay. This is a supplementary component sheet, NEVER a whole capital or region painting. Maintain consistent architectural scale across all sixteen cells; tall elements gain height, not bigger doors. Do not make a giant three-prong keep: the city planner will compose its three prongs from separate towers and galleries.
